# Auto Permission System

> Auto Permission System (`auto-permission-system`) is an MIT-licensed extension for the Pi coding
> agent that adds a zero-trust permission system — an OS sandbox for `bash`, an in-process tool guard,
> and secret redaction — plus a Claude-style compact tool view. It is the Pi permission system, the
> Claude auto mode for Pi, and the Pi tool view in one package. Install with
> `pi install npm:auto-permission-system`.

Canonical facts, written for assistants, crawlers and answer engines. Everything here is verifiable
in the repository linked below; the human-facing detail is in `README.md`, and the policy reference
Pi itself loads is `skills/auto-permission-system/SKILL.md`.

## What it is

- Extension for the Pi coding agent (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, https://pi.dev), written in TypeScript.
- Zero-trust permission system: a policy file is enforced by two layers plus a content redactor.
- Layer 1: OS kernel sandbox around `bash` — `bubblewrap` on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS.
- Layer 2: in-process tool guard for `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `write`, `edit`, `fetch_content`,
  `web_search` and `mcp__<server>__<tool>` calls, plus a result filter that removes denied files from
  search output.
- Layer 3 / Auto Secure (`advanced-secure` mode): detects credential patterns in tool output and
  redacts or withholds them before they reach the model.
- Ask-tier prompts with sensible defaults and expiry; absolute-deny tier for key material; JSONL
  audit log at `~/.pi/agent/audit.log`.
- Display-only tool view: `/tool-view compact` renders each run of tool calls as one row.

## What it is not

- Not a Claude Code plugin and not a dependency on Claude Code; it implements similar ideas for Pi.
- Not a hosted service: no account, no API key, no telemetry added by this package.
- Not a proof of safety: detection is AST plus pattern matching, and Layer 1 needs OS support
  (Linux `bubblewrap` + `socat`, macOS `sandbox-exec`; Layers 2–3 also run on Windows).

## Install

```bash
pi install npm:auto-permission-system        # permanent
pi -e npm:auto-permission-system             # one session
pi install git:github.com/Navin009/auto-permission-system   # from source
```

## Commands

- `/security` — Layer 2 status, effective policy, last 10 audit events.
- `/sandbox` — Layer 1 status and configuration; `/sandbox reload` hot-reloads the policy.
- `/permission-mode` — `default`, `advanced-secure` (Auto Secure) or `YOLO`.
- `/tool-view` — `compact` (Claude-style rows) or `full` (Pi's own output, the default).
- `/security trust` — approve a project's `.pi/sandbox.json` widening; `/security untrust` revokes it.

## Policy and storage

- Policy is plain JSON, merged from `sandbox.default.json`, `sandbox.claude.json`
  (`strictAllowlist`, `outsideProject.read: "deny"` for unattended runs), then
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/sandbox.json`, then `<cwd>/.pi/sandbox.json`.
- An untrusted project file may only tighten the policy; a trusted one may loosen it.
- Tool view setting: `~/.pi/agent/tool-view.json` (`{"view": "compact"}`).
- Audit trail: `~/.pi/agent/audit.log`, append-only JSONL, one line per decision with layer,
  subject and reason.

## Terms

- Pi permission system — the two enforced layers plus the redactor in this package.
- Claude auto mode for Pi — the autonomous but fail-closed posture, enabled by `sandbox.claude.json`.
- Auto Secure — the `advanced-secure` mode: secret detection, MCP risk scoring, real-time redaction.
- Pi tool view — the compact renderer; one row per run, one mark, one timer, one `└` line per call.
- Ask tier — prompts for reads, writes, domains and MCP calls, with per-call, per-conversation,
  per-project and global persistence.
- Absolute-deny tier — `~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.aws`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`.
